assessment_details.rationale: Concrete continual-learning implementation safety could matter if O adopts distributed regularizer-based adaptation, but the immediate bottleneck is recovery/context/effect execution.
Useful correctness discipline for adaptive evaluation abstractions, but particle-resampling mechanics are distant from O's current software-agent control path.
The ordering-sensitive variance failure is a transferable warning about correlated allocation randomness, but adapting it to O is nontrivial.
The result cautions that diversity metrics can be misleading, yet genealogy diagnostics have weak immediate fit to O's current bottleneck.
Predictable square-root allocation directly targets O's need to spend scarce evaluation/research effort where expected information value is highest.
The held-out 14% fixed-budget variance reduction plus reversed-allocation negative control is directly useful for falsifiable resource-allocation policy design.
Process-stable runtime identity is directly relevant to O's frozen Work requests, permits, restart behavior and exact continuation safety.
The import-time secret reload defect is a close analogue to O's requirement that execution identity stay stable within a process but fail closed across restart.
O's recursive Skill/context routing can become useless if relevant capabilities fail to enter the shortlist; registry-scale retrieval recall is directly decision-relevant.
O currently depends on monitors/recovery decisions; fixed-false-alarm lead time and observability are better intervention criteria than rank metrics alone.
O's safety depends on pre-effect authorization; distinguishing blocking from observation-only host hooks directly tests whether abstract policy has real control authority.
Provider contention and retry storms can stall O even with local concurrency caps; coordinated retry/backpressure is directly relevant to execution reliability.
O is actively repairing a stopped Work execution; calibrated causal attribution plus environment-verified repair is directly aligned with that bottleneck.
Typed, concrete repair affordances could shorten O's recovery loops and reduce unproductive diagnosis-only retries when authoritative state knows admissible fixes.
Structured failure taxonomies can improve reflection, but the reported effect is less isolated and less directly action-authoritative than literal repair affordances.
Selective intervention directly maps to O watchdog/advisor economics: maximize rescue while minimizing solved-to-unsolved disruption and model-call cost.
Intermediate repair suggestions are plausibly useful for O, but the SGAgent result is confounded by additional model compute and a multi-agent software-repair scaffold.
Verifier calls are expensive and correlated; class-conditional residual-value calibration can tell O when an extra evaluator is useless or harmful.
CAUSE is a promising uncertainty-attribution idea, but current O has no neural/restless-bandit substrate and adaptation would be substantial.
The calibrated identifiability/abstention learner is conceptually useful for distinguishing change from noise, but remains a synthetic window model far from O's control stack.
Abstain-to-shared-base is a general decision-safety pattern that could inform O when causal attribution is weak, though the evidence is synthetic bandit-specific.
Stable snapshot semantics matter for durable replay, but O's authority is primarily Git/CAS rather than a local rotating JSONL event store.
Retaining a verified incumbent while buying optional challenger compute maps directly to O's reversible candidate/strategy replacement policy and protected-regression requirement.
The failed preregistered holdout is valuable negative evidence for avoiding overconfident early VoC gates, though the domain is synthetic ROBDD search.
The successful sequential continuation rule is strong evidence for trajectory-conditioned compute buying under a retained incumbent, closely matching O's expected-time objective.
Nonzero audit support plus anytime-valid inference is directly relevant to O's held-out acceptance and avoiding blind spots in rejected strategy regions.
Finite-horizon continuation value and out-of-sample allocation cautions directly inform O's strategy/resource scheduler and evidence-cost accounting.
Stage-aware acquisition arbitration directly complements O's exploration-bias detection: first discriminate mechanisms, then refine only after calibrated confidence.
A write-ahead provider-effect journal addresses the exact hard-kill/remote-effect gap that O's own context/effect architecture still marks as unresolved.
